key_insight: A single multi-turn agent can learn to adapt resource use to user-specified budgets when training rewards penalise overspending.
engineering_relevance: Budget-aware training can improve resource control across tokens, API calls, and interaction steps without external budget-allocation controllers.
method: Compare 11 reward objectives, including adapted length penalties and new overspending penalties.
Train Qwen3.5 4B and 9B models across budget values, with separate policies for each environment and resource type.
Evaluate success within budget and natural compliance, including generalisation beyond training conditions.
evidence_signal: Experiments on AppWorld and BabyAI show gains over untrained and success-only baselines, extending to unseen budgets, a shifted task distribution, and a new benchmark.
watch_item: Reward choice trades off within-budget success against natural compliance; learned compliance should not be treated as a guaranteed hard resource cap.
paper_title: Rewards for Budget-Aware Multi-Turn Agents That Adapt to Arbitrary Test-Time Constraints
